subject: Anthropology
title: Digital Commons
description: A micro-lesson that makes Digital Commons usable.

hook.text: Wikipedia, open-source code, and Creative Commons. The internet has revived the idea of shared knowledge resources.

buildup.text: Digital commons are shared online resources — software, data, and knowledge — that anyone can access and contribute to.

discovery.text: Open-source projects like Linux prove that collective production can rival corporate products in quality and scale.

twist.text: Tech companies profit from the digital commons while enclosing them. Free data gets harvested and sold back to users.

climax.text: The digital commons are contested ground. The same internet that enables sharing also enables new forms of enclosure.

punchline.text: The battle between sharing and owning continues online.

quiz.question: What are digital commons?
options: Shared online resources anyone can access and contribute to

details.summary: Digital commons are shared digital resources — open-source software, Wikipedia, Creative Commons works — governed collaboratively outside market and state control. They represent a new form of communal production that challenges assumptions about private ownership as the only driver of innovation.
details.whyItMatters: Digital commons demonstrate that cooperation and sharing can produce remarkable innovation without private ownership incentives. They offer a model for managing knowledge as a shared resource rather than an excludable commodity.
takeaways: Digital commons include open-source software, Wikipedia, and shared works
They are governed collaboratively outside market and state control
They challenge private ownership as the only driver of innovation

faq.question: How do digital commons relate to traditional commons?
faq.answer: Both involve shared resources managed by communities through collective governance. Digital commons share the same logic as pastoral commons or fishing grounds — rules of access, contribution norms, and community monitoring.

faq.question: Are digital commons threatened by enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes. Expanding intellectual property laws, platform monopolies, paywalls, and data privatization enclose digital commons just as land enclosures destroyed agricultural commons. The struggle between open access and proprietary control is a defining economic conflict of the digital age.
